title: Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs
seoTitle: Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Crispy skin, lean protein, oven ease
subtitle: Crispy skin, lean protein, oven ease
description: Crispy skin, lean protein, oven ease. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Fresh thyme, Fresh rosemary, Kosher salt as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season and arrange
steps.instruction: Pat thighs dry; season under and over skin. Arrange skin-up on oiled sheet pans with space between pieces. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Roast until crisp
steps.instruction: Roast at 425°F 35–42 minutes until skin crackles and thickest part reads 165°F. Juices run clear when pierced. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and hold
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes. Hold on racks at 200°F — stacking steams skin soft. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Crisp skin under broiler
steps.instruction: If skin softened while holding, broil 1–2 minutes skin-up until crackly. Watch closely — thighs go from crisp to burnt fast. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Portion bowls on the line with protein visible on top — crew eats with their eyes first.
Keep dressing and crunchy toppings in side bowls so greens stay crisp through second servings.
Line up Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Crispy skin, lean protein, oven ease. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
